The described vulnerability (H-05) is a multi-bug exploit in Stop/Signer that hinges on: (a) stopRent/stopRentBatch reclaiming assets before verifying the order exists in storage, allowing a non‑existent RentalOrder to be supplied; (b) EIP‑712/signing issues (RentPayload not bound to a specific order; OrderMetadata omissions) enabling reuse of a generic signature; and (c) RentalOrder hash omitting rentalWallet, letting the attacker point reclaim at a victim safe. During onERC721/1155Received the attacker creates the matching order, so the later settlement/removal succeeds, resulting in theft of any actively rented NFT (including ERC721) and frozen escrow. 

The audit report does not describe this full chain or the decisive flaw that stopRent performs reclaim before checking order existence. While the report does flag related sub-issues — Protocol signature not bound to the Seaport order (Medium), OrderMetadata hash omitting fields (Medium), and rentalWallet omitted from the order hash (Medium) — it neither ties them together nor identifies the early reclaim/creation-on-callback path that enables theft of any NFT. Its rentalWallet omission finding focuses on an ERC1155-only cross‑rental corruption scenario and explicitly notes ERC721 generally reverts, which is different from H‑05’s universal theft path. Other High issues in the report (fallback handler gap, disableModule offset, Seaport tips) are different root causes and code paths. Fixing any single reported issue would not by itself fix H‑05. Therefore, the same vulnerability is not detected.
